sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.title: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'
sources.text: Rockstar made a point of creating "authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality." It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion. One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6 , Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained. Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world." This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts . And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
sources.text: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real." I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood. I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6 's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom. "A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer." Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there." While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. sources.title: GTA 6: Find and break into Freddie Gibbs’ doomsday compound in Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: How to find Freddie Gibbs, enter his compound, and get rewards in Grand Theft Auto 6 Rapper Freddie Gibbs is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and heâs a doomsday prepper with an impressive compound and bunker. Freddie is convinced that the apocalypse is coming, so heâs built up a doomsday bunker and compound, complete with an electric fence, mines, and even explosive drones. Thatâs just the defenses â heâs really prepared for the world to end. Freddie is a pretty nice and generous guy once you get to know him, but getting to know him isnât so easy. In this guide, weâre breaking down how to find and break into Freddieâs compound both times in GTA 6. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Freddieâs compound is located on the North shore of Lake Leonida in North Leonard County. Itâs on the same road as One-Eyed Willieâs Auto Shop (Ultimate Edition exclusive). You canât miss it as itâs a large compound surrounded by electric fences, and has multiple billboards propped up warning about the end of the world. The first time you break into Freddieâs compound, it has an obvious flaw. A water tower to the rear of the compound is outside of the electric fence. It has an unblocked ladder that you can climb to take you up to a platform, from which you can jump onto the roof of a shed inside the electric fence. You will have to watch out for both proximity mines and drones. Proximity mines will be highlighted in Focus mode, and when you hear a drone, Focus mode will again give you enough time to shoot them down. The best route through the compound is sticking close to the fence while heading East, and then South. Proximity mines will not be placed on the pipes and cables in the compound, meaning you can use them as a walkway. You will complete the challenge by getting to the front door of the large dug-out bunker. The first time you complete this challenge, Freddie will free you and challenge you to return later, after he improves his defenses. After some time, Freddie will text Jason and Lucia, challenging them to a rematch. You need to break into his compound and get to the door of his bunker again, only this time the water tower isnât an option, and the proximity mines and drones have been buffed. Nothing is impossible, though, and Jason and Lucia are both pretty good climbers who are able to clamber on top of large vehicles. You see where this is going. To the rear of the compound â the Northwest corner â youâll find a tractor with a large trailer, along with a bulldozer. Park the tractor and trailer along the fence, and then use the bulldozer to lift the trailer into the air. This will give you the perfect ramp to climb up the tractor, onto the trailer, and over the electric fence. Even Freddie wonât see it coming. Head to the bunker door again with the same route as last time â while watching out for more mines â and Freddie will finally emerge to greet you before inviting you inside. A storm will start, and you will have to choose between staying or leaving. If you leave, Freddie will give you $6,250 cash. As a reward for staying with him, Freddie will give you the valuable Benefactor Dubsta that you can register and keep.

sources.text: How to recover Jason’s Key Lento Rainy-Day Fund stash in Grand Theft Auto 6 Mild spoiler alert: you should at least make it to Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6 before reading on. Things go very wrong at the climax of GTA 6âs first chapter. Jason and Lucia will have to abandon their home in Key Lento, and the stash of cash and Jasonâs collection of photographs go with them. But you can go back. The stash under the floorboards has burned up, but the money and photographs in the metal box are still intact, and you can recover them. Only, thatâs easier said than done. In this guide, weâre breaking down the best way to recover Jasonâs stash and photographs in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. To reiterate the above: the money you stashed under the floorboards will have burned up, but Jason did put $5,000 away as a Rainy-Day Fund for his family. If you stored more than that under the floorboards, Iâm sorry to say that the money is sadly gone. Still, the $5,000 is worth recovering, and thereâs at least one nice surprise to see. Your stash is, of course, in the same building that burned up in Key Lento. Cops will be patrolling the nearby area, and theyâll be stationed in front of Jasonâs house and on the dock around back, meaning you canât simply drive up in either a car or boat. The best option is to get a RydeMe taxi to a nearby location on the North or East side of the zone the cops are patrolling, like Chuckâs Tackle and Shot or The Rusty Anchor. Make sure to wear a disguise â hat, sunglasses, bandana â and sneak through gardens to get to the building North of Jasonâs burned-out home, just over the small canal where boats can dock. Cops wonât be patrolling this side of the house, meaning you can dive into the water and swim over to the boat ramp near Jasonâs basketball hoop. The stairs immediately in front of the ramp are very close to a pair of cops out front, so circle around the North side of the house and use the other stairs. If you stop to look under the stairs, youâll find Jasonâs snake Dolores has made a nest and laid some eggs. A happy ending. Climbing the stairs, youâll easily be able to find the stash and metal tin in the same place as ever. Quickly recover both the money and photographs, and escape the same way you came in before getting outside of the patrol zone and changing your disguise. Congratulations, youâve got some of your money back.

sources.title: Steve Rogers returns to action in final Avengers: Doomsday trailer
sources.text: A new look at Avengers: Doomsday has dropped A new trailer for Avengers: Doomsday has been released, and it's our best look yet at the upcoming Marvel movie . The new teaser features Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom as he faces the Avengers, but firstly focuses on Steve Rogers' choice of a lifetime as he is visited by the Fantastic Four and leaves Peggy and their son behind. What follows is largely what has been in marketing to date, including the Sentinels being raised by Doom at the X-Mansion. But we get an extra cherry on top: Doomsday's own 'assembling' scene, featuring the X-Men, Captain America, Steve Rogers, and plenty more heroes besides. As one of the OG Avengers, Thor also does his level best to rally the troops, even throwing in a line that might resonate with casual audiences. "I don't even know who half of you are," he says at one point, but is still ready to team up with them against the universe-ending threat of Doom and the incursions. As the official synopsis teases, the heroes from three different universes will have to come together to face their biggest foe yet: Victor Von Doom. The Avengers, Wakandans, and New Avengers join with the Fantastic Four and the original X-Men, meaning the cast list features everyone from Chris Evans to Ian McKellen as more than 30 heroes line up on the battlefield. The new trailer comes after a week of big news for Doomsday. First of all, the VisionQuest finale revealed that Wanda Maximoff is returning for the big team-up movie after she was resurrected by the villain in a post-credits scene. Not only that, but Kevin Feige also debunked a pretty huge theory in a new interview with Empire magazine. "People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He's Victor Von Doom," Feige teased . Subscribe for a weekly digest of the movie and TV news that matters, direct to your inbox. From first-look trailers, interviews, reviews and explainers, we’ve got you covered. Just when we think we know what's happening, Feige debunks it... It seems like we'll just have to wait for the epic movie to arrive in theaters before we find out all of the secrets that Marvel has been holding in all this time. Avengers: Doomsday arrives in US theaters on December 18 and a few days earlier in the UK on December 16. For more on the MCU, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order . sources.text: Avengers: Doomsday is just under a month away, and we now have the final trailer. sources.title: Avengers: Doomsday’s Final Trailer Is Here, and It Finally Gives Us a Reason to Care
sources.text: Avengers: Doomsday is now just weeks away, and Marvel Studios continues to build hype with a new trailer for this year's highly anticipated Avengers sequel. The trailer offers the longest look yet at the movie, teasing several emotional hooks. We see Steve Rogers's life with Peggy and their young son, who was kept in the dark about Steve's past as Captain America. Perhaps most revealingly, we learn that Cap's decision to travel to the past has had unforeseen consequences when the Fantastic Four pay him a visit. Perhaps this is what Dr. Doom means when he refers to these characters living "stolen lives." The trailer ends with a callback to one of the Avengers series' best long-running bits as Cap asks Thor if the God of Thunder is bothered by the fact that Cap is holding his "former" hammer, Mjolnir. Additionally, we get more mutant action as Cyclops delivers the iconic "To me, my X-Men" line, summoning Nightcrawler along with Mystique and Gambit. If most of the film's teasers until now felt like they were mostly there to show off all the characters returning, this is the first one that felt like it offered a reason to care about this impending superpowered brawl. The latest trailer for Doomsday follows the first trailer released in July and an extended " special look " that emerged from Disney's D23 fan convention. After a series of middling box office showings for its superhero movies (Sony's Spider-Man: Brand New Day notwithstanding), Marvel Studios hopes to return to Avengers: Endgame -era glory with an all-star show of force that brings back characters from the past decade-plus of the MCU and the Fox era of X-Men films. Directors Joe and Anthony Russo return to Marvel with a mandate to revive the broad cultural interest (and box office) of their previous Avengers twofer. The next Avengers movie stars Robert Downey Jr. as Doctor Doom, Chris Hemsworth as Thor, Anthony Mackie as Captain America, Sebastian Stan as the Winter Soldier, Letitia Wright as Shuri, Paul Rudd as Ant-Man, Wyatt Russell as U.S. Agent, Tenoch Huerta Mejía as Namor, Vanessa Kirby as Sue Storm, Pedro Pascal as Mister Fantastic, Joseph Quinn the Human Torch, Ebon Moss-Bachrach as the Thing, Simu Liu as Shang-Chi, Florence Pugh as White Widow, Kelsey Grammer as the Beast, Lewis Pullman as Sentry, Danny Ramirez as Falcon, David Harbour as Red Guardian, Winston Duke as M'Baku, Hannah John-Kamen as Ghost, Tom Hiddleston as Loki, Patrick Stewart as Professor X, Ian McKellen as Magneto, Alan Cumming as Nightcrawler, Rebecca Romijn as Mystique, James Marsden as Cyclops, and Channing Tatum as Gambit. Avengers: Doomsday arrives in movie theaters on Dec. 18. sources.title: How to get a Snap Gun in GTA 6 to quietly lockpick doors
sources.text: The GTA 6 Snap Tool is an essential item which lets you get into locked doors without setting off alarms Breaking and entering is more complicated than it's ever been before in a Grand Theft Auto game. You never know what's behind a locked door – cash to be grabbed, narcotics to be fences, safes to be broken into. The problem is that breaking open doors creates a lot of noise, and will set off alarms. Thankfully, there is another way. All you need is to find the Snap Gun in GTA 6. The Snap Gun is a lockpicking device that can be acquired by progressing through the main story, and it's perhaps the most important piece of equipment in the game (beating out the Slim Jim and the Key Cloner ). Below I'm going to walk you through how to get the GTA 6 Snap Gun and how to use it. The Snap Gun is locked behind progression. You'll need to complete Yasmani's Jewelry Jobs in Chapter 3, a fence-specific GTA 6 mission that unlocks after you've completed Boobie Time. You'll be introduced to Yasmani, one of the key vendors in GTA 6 who will pay a premium for marked bills and jewellery you've stolen. He'll give you the Snap Gun so that Jason and Lucia can properly assist in a few heists of high-end jewellery stores in Vice City. If a door is locked, there's a very good chance that you can use the Snap Gun to open it. Walk up to a door and, rather than pressing Square/X to break it open, press Triangle/Y instead. This will let you use the Snap Gun, where you're then required to use the left analogue stick to find the sweet spot and then pump the right-trigger until a meter fills. You'll hear the click when the lock is picked. The Snap Gun is particularly useful when you're robbing Pawn Shops, Jewellery stores, and other key locations – so long as you've already threatened the clerks and guards to stay still while you work. The Snap gun circumvents alarm systems installed in stores to monitor the door. It's worth noting here that in certain locations that carry a lot of cash or valuables, a Snap Gun won't be enough. If you walk up to a door and it's only asking for explosives, then a sticky bomb or grenade is what's required – just prepared for the alarms to go off and for the cops to be in hot pursuit. sources.title: GTA 6 at 60fps is actually possible thanks to an Xbox Series X glitch
sources.text: Some GTA 6 hopefuls weren't chuffed when hearing the open-world crime fest is targeting 30fps on all consoles, but there's actually a way to circumvent that framerate cap thanks to a newly-discovered glitch on Xbox. Before the game's meteoric launch, Rockstar Games confirmed that its crime fest was locked at 30fps on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S - the studio acknowledged that even the PS5 Pro wasn't capable enough to simulate the game's massive, complicated world at higher framerates, either. But Redditor Mewwie64's has found a way to run the game with an unlocked framerate by using a Quick Resume glitch on Xbox Series X - that's the handy feature that lets you switch between games from where you last left off, without needing to boot up each one from scratch. To run GTA 6 at 60fps or higher, you'll apparently need a 120hz display, an Xbox Series X, and the game itself on version 01.002.001. "This glitch may still work on later versions," the Redditor says, "not sure." The dedicated player also gave interested folks a tutorial on how to up those framerate caps: "Put your Xbox display settings to 60hz. Start GTA 6. Wait until you see the six stars in the intro. Change your display settings back to 120hz. Cold boot another game on your console via the Xbox Guide (The Xbox button) and without quitting GTA 6. Switch back to GTA 6." And, voila. The Redditor does have one pretty big disclaimer, before you get too excited. "The game speed seems to be tied to your framerate," they write, so increasing the framerate might lead to certain animations looking faster than normal. "It seems like the animations are at 2x speed or more in Jason's house in Chapter 1. I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more. But when you exit the house everything runs at an increased speed (The game world is likely tied to your framerate) but cutscenes work 100% fine without issues on higher framerates. Only the gameplay is sped up." Be warned, then. sources.text: You can keep playing GTA 6 after the credits, but there's some things you may want to know first No matter how far you're through the main GTA 6 missions list , you are probably starting to get a sense of just how massive Leonida really is – and how stacked it is with curiosities, distractions, objectives, and side-activities. You can continue free-roam after beating GTA 6 , albeit with a few caveats. Because there are numerous GTA 6 endings, with a wide range of different variables and impacts for all of the characters depending on your relationship status , your criminal profile , whether you paid into family savings , and plenty more besides, Rockstar has decided that it would be far too difficult to simply drop you back into Vice City in a world in which there are no more main missions daunting your GTA 6 Index . This means that once you've completed the main story in GTA 6, the game will drop you back to an auto-save just before the point-of-no-return. When the game does this, I recommend that you be prepared to make a new save in GTA 6 – as that auto-save won't exist forever, and can be lost if you decide to load an old save or start the campaign over from scratch. From this point, you're free to do whatever you want to do. Your relationship status will be locked, so there's no need to worry about maintaining this if you don't want to, but you can still mess around with your Criminal Profile. You can also, at any point, restart the final mission and go through it again. The GTA 6 end-game is where the world really lets you be free. You'll have loads of GTA 6 challenges to complete, which contribute to the unlocking of GTA 6 Cheats that are now available in the Progress menu. Reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6 's frame-rate on Series X. Their hack relied on the Xbox's rarely-discussed Quick Resume feature, which lets you park multiple games in memory and switch between them without having to re-load each game. In a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch. For starters, you're going to need a 120Hz monitor display or TV, as the glitch requires adjusting refresh rates. First, you need to limit Xbox to display at 60Hz under the console Settings menu. Then, you start GTA 6 (version 01.002.001), wait until the six-star logo appears and then go back to Xbox Settings to change the refresh rate to 120Hz. Before you return to GTA 6, the final step requires launching another game on your console. This has to be a cold boot, meaning the game shouldn't already be running parked in Quick Resume. After the second game launches, you now need to use Quick Resume to resume playing GTA 6, which is when you're going to notice the higher frame-rate. The Reddit user said the game could reach 90-plus FPS at certain moments. Unfortunately, the user also discovered that game-speed appears to be tied to frame-rate in GTA 6, at least when it comes to certain gameplay animations and when performing certain actions. "I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more," Meowwie64 wrote. Incidentally, cutscenes do not appear to be affected by this issue, so they run at their normal speed. As much as a 30fps frame-rate makes GTA 6 feel less smooth and potentially less enjoyable to play compared to 60fps or higher, none of the current-generation consoles are capable of delivering frame-rates beyond that. Tech experts Digital Foundry recently explained why even the PS5 Pro isn't powerful enough to run the game at 60fps or even 40fps.

sources.title: This '90s-inspired horror game has one of the coolest post-apocalyptic worlds I've ever seen
sources.text: Plus you can experience it all from the comfort of your campervan. I often find myself thinking where the best place to survive a zombie apocalypse would be. A walled-off stone house would certainly make for some good defenses, a boat would be great—but only if the zombies didn't pull a Fear the Walking Dead—or you could spend the end of the world in a camper van. That would certainly be whimsical. You do just this in The Road of Dust and Sorrow's demo , although it's certainly not as whimsical as I first imagined it to be. You see, in this 2D horror game you have bigger responsibilities than just keeping yourself alive, you also have a young daughter to look out for as well. This isn't an easy task. Supplies are dwindling, zombie-like humans infected by addictive chemicals amble across the land in search of more dust, but they'll settle for your blood instead. Plus there's this creepy Pastor who's definitely up to something very bad. I only got one glimpse of him in the demo and he was surrounded by a lot of gore and eldritch horror, so I've just decided that staying away from him is probably for the best. But you can't hunker down and forget about all these terrors, because you have a daughter to feed and protect. So I spent most of my time in the demo gathering food, medical supplies, and trying to locate an item that may just grant us safe passage to the only sanctuary humanity has left. The dev, Painted Black Games, says it took inspiration from horror series like Silent Hill and Resident Evil for The Road of Dust and Sorrow, and while I haven't come across anything particularly traumatic in a Silent Hill sense yet (although I wouldn't be surprised to see that here) I can see the through line to Resident Evil. The action is smooth, accurate, and rewarding—which surprised me as I usually don't vibe with 2D gunplay, sometimes the controls are too finicky, but it certainly works here. Head-shotting the zombies is incredibly satisfying, as is kicking them to the floor and beating them with a baseball bat. Then there are the puzzles. I didn't come across too many, but the ones I did find were very rewarding. It's not rocket science, but the solutions aren't always obvious either. They are, however, very intuitive; you can do a lot with a little, something I very much appreciate. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. But my favourite aspect of The Road of Dust and Sorrow has to be just how cool this post-apocalyptic world is. Maybe it's the pixel art, but it manages to look dilapidated and creepy while also being oddly pretty to look at. I was searching an abandoned warehouse full of zombies and rotting cargo while thinking to myself that with a bit of elbow grease this place could really scrub up. If you want pretty and cosy, though, the campervan is where it's at. I didn't spend as much time as I would have liked to there, but it managed to feel like a real home—the only safe place left in this world. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Elie is a news writer with an unhealthy love of horror games—even though their greatest fear is being chased. When they're not screaming or hiding, there's a good chance you'll find them testing their metal in metroidvanias or just admiring their Pokemon TCG collection. Elie has previously worked at TechRadar Gaming as a staff writer and studied at JOMEC in International Journalism and Documentaries – spending their free time filming short docs about Smash Bros. or any indie game that crossed their path. sources.text: On its 25th anniversary, the developers behind Segaâs cult classic tell its story – and reveal why its sequel was cancelled Itâs August 2024. I’m riding through the neon-soaked streets of Tokyoâs Shibuya Ward in a Porsche, with the director of one of my favorite games at the wheel. We’re heading to his home, where he’s promised to show me beta builds that have never been seen before, and details on its canned sequel. There’s no shortage of hard work involved in covering video games, but every so often you have one of those days that makes you stop and think: wow, I’m lucky to do this. This was one of them. For me, Rez was a revelatory experience that arrived during a formative moment in my life. I was about to turn 16, leave school, and enter a hedonistic life of clubbing, music, and the human connection that comes with it. At the same time, my gaming habits had broadened into a more eclectic mix of multiplatform games, with publications like Edge encouraging me to think more about them as an artistic medium. It was inevitable, then, that I’d eventually take a chance on an electric arthouse shooter from the arcade masters at Sega . I went in blind, and discovering its abstract wireframes and interactive techno beats for myself was a deeply affecting experience. It was like simultaneously conducting a Chemical Brothers album and the Ministry of Sound light show, behind the controls of a Space Harrier machine, in a combo only video games could power. To view Rez as simply a shooter is to completely miss its meaning. On the surface, it shares much with on-rails arcade games like Panzer Dragoon and Star Fox , tasking players with blasting their way through waves of enemies on route to a spectacular boss. But these familiar mechanics are a vehicle for something more transcendent. UGAâs young team were trying to do something few commercially developed games had attempted before. Rezâs central concept is synaesthesia, the phenomenon of one sensory experience triggering another, like sounds provoking certain shapes and colors. The player is treated as a participant in a performance, with the gameâs licensed music responding to every dispatched enemy with a hi-hat or synthesizer, like you’re some sort of Tron-age conductor. All the while, its pulsing, Kandinsky-inspired visuals move in harmony with the audio, and your game controller passes the vibrations through your body, as if youâve plugged the Dreamcast into your own auxiliary port. There was simply nothing else like Rez at the time. It isn’t hyperbole to say that United Game Artists’ extraordinary sensory alchemy fundamentally changed how I, and many others of a similar age, viewed video games and what they could be. Its sales werenât spectacular, but Rezâs cultural impact makes it as valuable as any blockbuster. “It isn’t hyperbole to say that United Game Artists’ extraordinary sensory alchemy fundamentally changed how I, and many others of a similar age, viewed video games and what they could be.” Rez mattered because it showed, at a time when creators were obsessed with emulating Hollywood, that video games could create experiences that other entertainment mediums couldnât replicate. With its Y2K-inspired aesthetic, arcade-coded design, and deep reverence for late 90s club culture, Rez is staunchly a creation of its time, but itâs also absolutely timeless. To this day, Iâll regularly throw some headphones on, or a VR headset, and blast through Area 3, with its thumping Ken Ishii techno, or if Iâm in a more energetic mood, the evolutionary rollercoaster of Adam Freelandâs finale, and go beyond synaesthesia. âI do think as time has marched on, the game has become more celebrated and dear to people than when it was originally released,â producer Tetsuya Mizuguchi tells me in a meeting room at his latest studio, Enhance (he wasnât the one driving the car, by the way â weâll get to that later). âWhen we were making it too, towards the end of development, it felt more like the start of something than the end of a project for me personally, but I didn’t really know what it was the start of. I think in many ways, because it was this primitive experience, because it didn’t fit exactly into one genre convention, perhaps one of the reasons it took some time for the adulation to come to the fore has a lot to do with it took people some time to find the words that allowed them to accurately describe what they liked about the experience.â It wasnât just the players who struggled to verbalize what that Rez experience meant, Mizuguchi says. âLooking back at myself and the development team, we had trouble when we were making it, trying to express what the team was and what we were after. âBack then, we’d spend a lot of time doing things like going to electronic music clubs and observing the crowds there, and the kind of different types of reactions they’d have as music would change, and what would move them, and trying to kind of pick up clues from that sort of reaction and human experience that we were trying to then apply into Rez. âBecause we were young, because we were fairly inexperienced, we were really operating a lot more off of intuition about what this game was going to become and how we were going to get there and what we were borrowing from these sort of observed human experiences. And so, in that sense, not just for the players, but for ourselves, it’s kind of taken these 25 years to better define what we were trying to go after and what made it special.â Mizuguchi describes the circumstances surrounding Rez’s development as something of a ‘perfect storm’, much of which was deliberately engineered. stories.title: Rockstar Says Jason's Viral Personality in GTA 6 Comes From Steve McQueen and Real-Life Veterans
stories.summary: Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Rockstar Says Jason's Viral Personality in GTA 6 Comes From Steve McQueen and Real-Life Veterans
sources.text: Rockstar Games has opened up about GTA 6 protagonist Jason's viral personality and the two specific inspirations that helped bring him to life. As 13 years of waiting for the next Grand Theft Auto ended last week, players have found themselves enamored with Jason Duval. Stoic, nonchalant, calm, composed, resigned; whatever you want to call one of GTA 6's new protagonists, Rockstar says it carefully crafted his already iconic demeanor by pulling from a Steve McQueen classic and real-life veterans. The studio's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, talked about how the studio behind the mega-hit video game built Jason from the ground up during a conversation with Destructoid . Centering the story on a "couple on the run" marked new territory for Rockstar, but it's far from a new concept in entertainment. So, the team turned to movies, particularly Sam Peckinpah's The Getaway. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone," Humphries explained. "We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." He continued, saying that Rockstar's research into real-world veterans and Army Rangers helped refine its approach. Those who have played the game (and keen-eyed trailer watchers ) already know about Jason's military background, so the influence here definitely tracks. "These guys typically aren’t running their mouths or reacting to something unless it’s strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves." Jason is the talk of Vice City and has been for some time. As Rockstar shared more details about its seemingly shy lead ahead of GTA 6's launch, some fans began to wonder if he could be the franchise's first-ever neurodivergent protagonist . In addition to his personality, Humphries described Jason as "wired differently" during a recent interview with Love magazine. While Jason steals more than just wads of cash in Vice City, his partner in crime has proven to be just as impactful. Game writer Michael Wiafe said looking into the kind of criminal activity known to make headlines in Florida was one of the first things the team did when creating both Jason and Lucia. For Rockstar, it wasn't just about creating true-to-life criminals; it was about creating fully realized human beings. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn’t stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What’s important is how they resonate, no matter where you’re experiencing the game in the world." Between the chaos of robbing gas stations and drug dealers and getting into high-speed car chases, Jason and Lucia can become quite the power couple. Game writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern said to Destructoid, "You really want them to make it." The quiet moments where the duo scrolls through social media in their bed or drives the other one to work can be just as important as the action set pieces. Gauvey-Kern added, "Those need to hit too, and you need to connect with how the characters are feeling in those moments." Although GTA 6 launched for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S three days ago, Leonida is packed with enough things to do to keep players playing for months. While we wait to see what's next for Rockstar, you can check out IGN's 10/10 review . You can also read about how the developers made every NPC feel like real people you could run into on the street . Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map . Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. sources.title: GTA 6's strong and silent Jason was inspired by Steve McQueen and former Army Rangers, says Rockstar
sources.text: If you've noticed that Grand Theft Auto 6's Jason Duval isn't much of a talker, that's by design, as his quiet nature was inspired by Steve McQueen and the studio's research into former Army Rangers. Speaking to Destructoid over email, Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative, Rupert Humphries, explained that the team looked at classic couple-on-the-run films when it decided on GTA 6's story. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was Peckinpah's The Getaway ," Humphries said. "Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." That approach also fitted the studio's research into veterans. "This also resonated with the research we were doing around veterans and particularly former Army Rangers (in our world we call them Marauders)," Humphries continued. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves." Game writer Michael Wiafe said Florida's real-life crime stories were "an obvious starting point" for GTA 6's characters more broadly. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe said. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn't necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don't attempt to make excuses for them." Fellow writer Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern added that while "the story takes some pretty heavy turns", Jason and Lucia's goal remains consistent. "So sharing their sense of determination, the focus on their goal, through all the highs and lows - that's what I hope people feel more than anything. You really want them to make it." GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day , not everyone is happy: some players have been review bombing its Metacritic user score over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda. Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review . If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats . Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort .

sources.title: GTA 6 "girlfriend simulator" complaints "are real" at first, ex-Rockstar lead says
sources.text: Obbe Vermeij says he's "having loads of fun now" he's further into the game One former Rockstar Games lead has a revolutionary take about GTA 6 – "it is good." But even though that may be the case, he reckons that "the complaints are real" in Chapter 1 from those suggesting that it "doesn't feel like a sandbox" and instead feels like a "girlfriend simulator." Obbe Vermeij worked at Rockstar Games between 1995 and 2009, serving as technical director on GTA 3, 4, Vice City, and San Andreas. Obviously, he'd left the studio well before GTA 6 started development (it might have been a long time coming, but it wasn't that long), so he's been playing through it alongside the rest of us. "It is good. Very good," he begins in a post on Twitter . However, there's a "but" coming. "In chapter 1 (The first 8 hours or so) the game doesn't give you much choice," he continues. "There are many tutorials, cut scenes, mandatory missions and the missions are basic. The complaints are real (realism over gameplay, girlfriend simulator, doesn't feel like a sandbox)." Opinions here do vary – I've definitely seen more than a few social media posts complaining about the optional tasks of grocery shopping for Lucia and buying her flowers, for example. They probably weren't high up the list of activities fans who planned to enter Leonida and immediately commit heinous crimes had in mind, I suppose – though it's worth keeping in mind that, again, those parts are optional. Equally, though, I've seen plenty of people enjoying the almost life-sim-esque vibe of GTA 6's opening hours, and that's probably reflected in how much time people spend in that first chapter. As someone who spent 18 hours in Chapter 1, you can probably guess what camp I fall into. Regardless, though, Vermeij reckons things really pick up by the time you reach the second chapter. "In chapter 2, the game backs off and gives you a bunch of missions to choose from," he says. "This is when the GTA magic kicks in." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Vermeij says he's now 46% of the way through the story in Chapter 3 and "having loads of fun now." He concludes that the "production values are unreal," and I don't think anyone could disagree with that. GTA 6 review s have been glowing across the board, and Rockstar has already achieved almost unfathomable commercial success, with a whopping 32.5 million copies sold via pre-orders (eclipsing a figure that took Elden Ring three years to reach) and earning $3.79 billion on day one. It had the biggest entertainment launch in history – I don't think the devs could have hoped for anything better. sources.text: Domingo é dia da nossa lista de lançamentos de jogos, para que você possa programar a sua agenda nos próximos dias. E o destaque dessa vez é Arkheron , game desenvolvido por um dos criadores de World of Warcraft e que mistura elementos de ação em tempo real com estratégia e coleta de itens ao longo das fases. Outro destaque é Appulse. O game conta com uma proposta ousada de misturar elementos de ação em tempo real, mais precisamente no controle de naves, a uma espécie de mesa de pinball interativa. Confira a lista completa de lançamentos da semana e os respectivos preços. Athelan Battlegrounds é um jogo de estratégia tática por turnos desenvolvido por uma equipe independente de duas pessoas. A proposta mistura elementos de xadrez com mecânicas de jogos competitivos em arenas, colocando os jogadores para montar equipes e disputar partidas estratégicas contra outros oponentes online. O título aposta em um sistema competitivo baseado apenas na habilidade dos participantes , sem mecânicas de progressão que ofereçam vantagens fora das partidas ou recursos pagos que influenciem o resultado. O game será distribuído de forma gratuita no PC através do Steam e já conta com uma versão demo para download. Appulse é um jogo de tiro com visão superior inspirado nas mecânicas clássicas de pinball. Ambientado no espaço, você precisa assumir o controle de uma nave e, assim, dominar o recuo das armas para controlar a trajetória da esfera pelo tabuleiro enquanto protege sua nave-mãe contra ondas de robôs invasores. A cada nível alcançado, é possível escolher melhorias para personalizar o arsenal, as habilidades e os recursos da mesa , além de utilizar um canhão de ejeção para invadir naves inimigas e cumprir objetivos específicos. O jogo ainda não possui um preço definido, mas já conta com uma versão demo disponível de forma gratuita. Arkheron é um jogo de ação isométrico focado em partidas competitivas entre equipes. A dinâmica consiste em escalar uma torre ao lado de dois aliados, enfrentando outros grupos de jogadores e coletando equipamentos pelo caminho que alteram as habilidades e a forma de jogar no meio dos combates. O título, que foi desenvolvido pelo veterano de World of Warcraft , Rob Pardo, também contará com um visual repleto de detalhes, além de um sistema de ranqueamento para possíveis torneios no futuro.
